dedupe_keys.name: replica seasonal trip tables synthetic population and network link volumes united states

description: Replica organises data about the built environment for transport decisions by public agencies and private companies. Its core product is a seasonal simulation of the whole population of the United States and its travel. Coverage: nationwide, split into megaregions of 10 to 50 million residents; the seasonal trip table has one row per trip for a typical Thursday and a typical Saturday of each season, with origin, destination, mode, purpose, routing and duration, linked by person, household, activity and route IDs to a synthetic population table with age, race and ethnicity, income, home and work or school locations; mode-specific tables cover auto and ride-hailing, transit, active transport and commercial freight trips. Documentation also describes network links and daily and annual link volumes, annual average daily traffic, free-flow and quarter-hourly speeds per link, daily origin-destination data and vehicle miles travelled, turning movement counts, transit routes, crash data, land use parcels, consumer spending flows, and scenario models for road closures. Format and access: the Replica web platform and direct database access; trip tables released twice a year and downloadable as CSV, bought as a whole or by mode; a sample trip table is downloadable from the documentation. Licence: commercial; not read. Caveats: trips are modelled outputs of a calibrated travel demand simulation, not observed trips; prices were not read. Simulation uses: synthetic population and trip tables for agent-based and network flow transport models, link volumes and speeds for calibration, and road closure scenarios for resilience and emergency response studies. Related records: TomTom traffic analytics (data-tomtom-maps-traffic-and-move-portal) for observed speeds.
